title: Abstract & professional topics vocabulary
blurb: Build the abstract, professional-register vocabulary — society, environment, technology, culture — that CCE-B2 reading passages assume you already know.

vocab.example: Moderní společnost čelí mnoha výzvám.
Musíme chránit životní prostředí pro další generace.
Udržitelnost je dnes klíčovým tématem v hospodářství.
Technologický rozvoj mění způsob, jakým pracujeme.
Hospodářství země roste už třetí rok po sobě.
Globalizace usnadňuje obchod mezi zeměmi.
Každý má právo na vlastní názor.
Dopad klimatických změn je čím dál patrnější.

grammarNote.title: Abstract nouns from adjectives & verbs: the -ost / -ství pattern
grammarNote.text: CCE-B2 reading passages lean heavily on abstract nouns built from adjectives and verbs, and recognizing the pattern makes unfamiliar words easier to decode on the fly. The suffix -ost turns an adjective into an abstract noun of quality, always feminine: udržitelný (sustainable) → udržitelnost (sustainability), možný (possible) → možnost (possibility), schopný (capable) → schopnost (ability). The suffix -ství/-ctví similarly builds abstract nouns, often for fields, states, or institutions, and is neuter: hospodářský (economic) → hospodářství (economy), přátelský (friendly) → přátelství (friendship). A third common pattern turns a verb stem into a process noun with -ní/-tí: vzdělávat (to educate) → vzdělávání (education), rozvíjet (to develop) → rozvoj (development, an irregular but very frequent case). Spotting these suffixes lets you infer the meaning of a word you've never seen from a root you already know — exactly the skill B2 reading passages test.

check.prompt: Which suffix most reliably turns a Czech adjective into an abstract noun meaning a quality or state?
check.explanation: -ost is the standard suffix for building feminine abstract nouns from adjectives: udržitelný → udržitelnost.
check.note: Watch for this pattern throughout B2 reading passages — it's one of the fastest ways to decode unfamiliar vocabulary.

check.prompt: „Hospodářství“ is a neuter noun meaning "economy," built from the adjective hospodářský with the -ství suffix.
check.explanation: Correct — hospodářský (economic) + -ství gives hospodářství (economy), a neuter abstract noun.
check.note: -ství/-ctví nouns are almost always neuter, unlike -ost nouns which are always feminine.

check.prompt: Text má velký ___ na to, jak lidé přemýšlejí o klimatu. (impact)
check.explanation: Dopad means "impact/effect" — a common abstract noun in discussions of environment and society.

check.prompt: Turn the adjective možný (possible) into the abstract noun meaning "possibility" using the -ost pattern: možný → ___
check.explanation: Adding -ost to the adjective stem možn- gives možnost (possibility), following the same pattern as udržitelný → udržitelnost.

title: Reading strategy: matching & gap-in-text
blurb: Learn the specific technique for CCE-B2 Úloha 1 and Úloha 3 — reconstructing paragraph order and matching titles to text — using cohesive-device clues instead of guesswork.

vocab.example: Co se týče ceny, ta zůstává stejná.
Na druhou stranu je potřeba zmínit i rizika.
Z tohoto důvodu firma změnila strategii.
Kromě toho stoupají i ceny energií.
Jak již bylo zmíněno, situace se rychle mění.
V neposlední řadě je třeba myslet na budoucí generace.
Naopak mladí lidé o tom problému moc nevědí.
Proto je důležité o tom mluvit včas.

grammarNote.title: Matching & gap-in-text: read for cohesion, not vocabulary
grammarNote.text: Úloha 1 (matching titles to paragraphs) and Úloha 3 (reconstructing the correct order of a scrambled text) don't test whether you understood every word — they test whether you can track how a text holds together. Two clues matter most. First, cohesive devices: connectors like na druhou stranu, kromě toho, z tohoto důvodu, and proto signal how one sentence relates to the next (contrast, addition, cause, consequence) — a paragraph opening with naopak almost never comes first, since it needs something to contrast with. Second, reference chains: pronouns (ten, ta, to, tam) and phrases like jak již bylo zmíněno point backward to something already introduced, so a paragraph using them can't be the opening paragraph either. For title-matching, skim for the paragraph's key noun phrase rather than reading every sentence — titles are usually built from a paraphrase of that noun phrase, not a literal repeat of it, so expect synonyms rather than exact matches. Practically: find the paragraph with no backward-pointing pronoun and no contrastive opener first (that's your anchor, usually the introduction), then chain the rest by matching connectors and pronouns to what precedes them.

check.prompt: A paragraph opening with „naopak“ (on the contrary) is most likely to be:
options: The very first paragraph of the text
A paragraph following one that made a contrasting point
A paragraph with no connection to the rest
check.explanation: Naopak signals contrast with something already stated, so it needs a preceding paragraph to contrast against — it can't open the text.
check.note: This is the core trick for Úloha 3: contrastive and backward-pointing connectors rule out the opening position.

check.prompt: In title-matching tasks (Úloha 1), the correct title usually repeats the paragraph's key phrase word-for-word.
check.explanation: Ne — titles are usually a paraphrase using synonyms, not a literal repeat, so scanning for exact word matches will mislead you.
check.note: Practice recognizing synonyms for common CCE-B2 topics (e.g., životní prostředí ↔ ekologie ↔ příroda) rather than only exact-word scanning.

check.prompt: ___ je nutné zmínit i to, kolik to bude stát. (besides that / in addition)
check.explanation: Kromě toho (besides that) signals an additive connection, adding a new point to what came before.

check.prompt: Rewrite to signal contrast instead of addition: „Kromě toho stoupají i ceny energií.“ → using naopak: ___
check.explanation: Swapping the additive kromě toho for the contrastive naopak changes the logical relationship the sentence signals to the previous one.

title: Reading strategy: true/false & implicit meaning
blurb: Master the CCE-B2 Úloha 4 technique — telling apart what a text states, what it contradicts, and what it simply doesn't mention.

vocab.translation: it follows from the text that
vocab.example: Z textu vyplývá, že situace se zlepšuje.
Text neuvádí, kolik lidí se akce zúčastnilo.
Tvrzení je v rozporu s tím, co autor napsal dříve.
Autor naznačuje, že řešení existuje.
Autor to doslova nenapsal, ale je to zřejmé.
Podle textu je problém vážnější, než se zdálo.
Z textu nelze usoudit, kdo za to nese odpovědnost.
Je zřejmé, že autor s tímto názorem nesouhlasí.

grammarNote.title: True/false/not-stated: telling contradicted apart from not-stated
grammarNote.text: Úloha 4 gives statements about a text and asks whether each is true, false, or (in some versions) not stated at all — and the exam's favorite trap is confusing false (contradicted) with not-stated (simply absent). A statement is false only if the text says the opposite or something logically incompatible with it — you should be able to point to the sentence that clashes with it. A statement is not stated when the text never addresses the topic at all, even if the claim sounds plausible or is common knowledge — no amount of world knowledge should let you mark it true or false, since the task tests reading, not general knowledge. The phrase text neuvádí (the text doesn't state) or z textu nelze usoudit (one cannot conclude from the text) describes this not-stated case precisely. A third pattern to recognize is implicit meaning: some correct statements are never said doslova (literally, word for word) but still follow logically — z textu vyplývá, že… (it follows from the text that…) — and you're expected to draw that inference the way you would in your own language, just more carefully, since B2 passages often bury the implication in a subordinate clause rather than stating it directly.

check.prompt: A statement is „not stated“ (rather than false) when:
options: The text says the exact opposite of the statement
The text never addresses that topic at all
The statement uses different words than the text
check.explanation: Not-stated means the text is simply silent on that point — false requires an actual contradiction in the text.
check.note: This is the single most common trap in Úloha 4: don't use outside knowledge to mark something true or false if the text itself never raises it.

check.prompt: If a statement is „v rozporu s“ (in contradiction with) the text, it should be marked false, not not-stated.
check.explanation: Correct — contradiction means the text actively disagrees with the statement, which is exactly what "false" means in this task.
check.note: Look for the specific sentence that clashes with the statement before marking anything false — a vague sense of disagreement isn't enough.

check.prompt: Autor to ___ nenapsal, ale z kontextu je to jasné. (literally)
check.explanation: Doslova (literally/word for word) marks the contrast between what's explicitly written and what's only implied.

check.prompt: Rewrite to express that a conclusion cannot be drawn from the text: „Víme, kolik lidí přišlo.“ → „Z textu ___, kolik lidí přišlo.“
check.explanation: Nelze usoudit (one cannot conclude) is the standard phrase for flagging that information isn't available in the text.
